Read and cut the transcript trees of TreeTerminus

Source: R/treeterminus.R
treeterminus.Rd

TreeTerminus builds, from Salmon replicates, a forest of transcript trees: the leaves are transcripts and every internal node is the sum of the transcripts below it, built so that the inferential uncertainty falls as the tree is ascended. Unlike the flat groups of Terminus, a tree lets the resolution change from one isoform to the next: an isoform the reads determine stays a leaf, one they do not is replaced by the smallest node that they do determine.

  • read_treeterminus() reads the trees (Newick, one per line): cluster_nwk.txt for the trees of all samples (treeterminus group --mean_inf true), group_nwk.txt for one sample, or the output of treeterminus consensus. TreeTerminus labels the leaves with the 0-based position of the transcript in quant.sf; salmon_dir (any of the Salmon directories, which share the order) or transcripts turns them into transcript IDs.

  • cut_transcript_trees() computes the inferential relative variance of every node from the replicates stored in an IsoformicExperiment (the draws of the transcripts below the node are summed), replaces every transcript whose own variance is at least cutoff by its lowest ancestor below cutoff, and returns the groups, which do not overlap (when two chosen nodes are nested, the larger one is kept). The result goes to add_uncertainty(groups = ), so that the confidence classes and collapse_groups work at the resolution the data support.

Transcripts whose whole path to the root stays above the cutoff are unresolved: by default they are left as they are (unresolved = "transcript"), where the confidence classes still flag them as uncertain; unresolved = "root" merges every tree that has one into a single group.

Usage

read_treeterminus(
  path,
  salmon_dir = NULL,
  transcripts = NULL,
  ignore_after_bar = TRUE
)

cut_transcript_trees(
  trees,
  x,
  cutoff = NULL,
  unresolved = c("transcript", "root")
)

Arguments

path

A Newick file of TreeTerminus, or a folder holding cluster_nwk.txt (or a single group_nwk.txt).

salmon_dir

A Salmon output directory quantified against the same index, whose quant.sf gives the order of the transcripts.

transcripts

Alternatively, the transcript names in quant.sf order.

ignore_after_bar

Logical. Keep only the part of transcript names before the first |.

trees

The result of read_treeterminus().

x

An IsoformicExperiment with inferential replicates (see add_uncertainty()).

cutoff

Inferential relative variance below which a node is well determined (the inf_rv_cutoff of add_uncertainty() by default).

unresolved

"transcript" or "root", see above.

Value

read_treeterminus(): a tibble with one row per node and leaf: tree_id, node_id (internal nodes; NA for leaves), transcript_id (leaves; NA for nodes) and parent_id (NA for the roots). cut_transcript_trees(): a tibble with transcript_id, group_id, group_size, group_inf_rv and tree_id for the transcripts that are grouped, with the cutoff in the cutoff attribute.

References

Singh NP, Love MI, Patro R (2023). TreeTerminus: creating transcript trees using inferential replicate counts. iScience 26(6):106961.

See also

read_terminus_groups(), add_uncertainty()

Examples

nwk <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
writeLines(c("((0,1),2);", "(3,4);"), nwk)
read_treeterminus(nwk, transcripts = c("tA1", "tA2", "tA3", "tB1", "tB2"))
#> # A tibble: 8 × 4
#>   tree_id node_id transcript_id parent_id
#>     <int>   <int> <chr>             <int>
#> 1       1       1 NA                   NA
#> 2       1       2 NA                    1
#> 3       1      NA tA1                   2
#> 4       1      NA tA2                   2
#> 5       1      NA tA3                   1
#> 6       2       3 NA                   NA
#> 7       2      NA tB1                   3
#> 8       2      NA tB2                   3
